## AI / Coding-Agent Artifact Investigation — `ansible/ansible` @ `45df14a2`

### Summary of findings

No generative-AI tooling (Copilot, ChatGPT, LLM prompts, generated-content disclosures) is present anywhere in this revision. What **is** present is a well-documented **traditional bot automation** system (`ansibullbot`), whose fingerprints span multiple artifact types.

---

### Candidate Observations

#### OBS-1 — `ansibullbot` process-automation bot, explicitly named and linked

**Artifact:** All three GitHub Issue Templates (bug, feature, docs) share an identical closing markdown block:

> *"Please, complete all sections as described, this form is processed automatically by a robot \[ansibot help\]."*
> Link: `/ansible/ansibullbot/blob/master/ISSUE_HELP.md#for-issue-submitters`

**Files:**
- [`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml` L245–252](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/ansible-ansible@45df14a2e05573e6213ce789aa3278f4f30fa54f/-/blob/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.yml?L245-252)
- [`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml` L167–179](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/ansible-ansible@45df14a2e05573e6213ce789aa3278f4f30fa54f/-/blob/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.yml?L167-179)
- [`.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/documentation_report.yml` L181–188](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/ansible-ansible@45df14a2e05573e6213ce789aa3278f4f30fa54f/-/blob/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/documentation_report.yml?L181-188)

**Interpretation:** Issues are fed to a named automation robot (`ansibullbot`). The bot parses structured template fields to drive triage, labelling, and routing — a form of structured-input-to-automation pipeline. No generative AI is involved.

---

#### OBS-2 — `BOTMETA.yml` — machine-readable bot configuration controlling ownership, routing, and suppression

**Artifact:** [`.github/BOTMETA.yml`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/ansible-ansible@45df14a2e05573e6213ce789aa3278f4f30fa54f/-/blob/.github/BOTMETA.yml)

Key fields at the top level:

```yaml
automerge: false
collection_redirect: true
notifications: false
```

The file maps file paths to bot-controlled metadata — `maintainers`, `labels`, `support`, `ignored`, `notified`, `keywords` — consumed by `ansibullbot` to automate PR triage, reviewer assignment, and notifications.

**Notable entries:**
- [`automerge: false`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/ansible-ansible@45df14a2e05573e6213ce789aa3278f4f30fa54f/-/blob/.github/BOTMETA.yml?L1) — automerge is explicitly **disabled** for the whole repo.
- [`ignored`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/ansible-ansible@45df14a2e05573e6213ce789aa3278f4f30fa54f/-/blob/.github/BOTMETA.yml?L16) fields on `$modules` and specific modules suppress bot-driven routing for those paths.
- `.github/BOTMETA.yml` is itself [tagged `labels: botmeta`, `support: core`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/ansible-ansible@45df14a2e05573e6213ce789aa3278f4f30fa54f/-/blob/.github/BOTMETA.yml?L59-61), meaning the bot monitors changes to its own configuration.

**Interpretation:** This is the primary bot-governance artifact. It is the closest thing in this repo to an "agent instruction file" — it constrains the bot's behavior, assigns human owners, and declares what the bot should suppress.

---

#### OBS-3 — Azure Pipelines "Bot Results" artifact publishing step

**Artifact:** [`.azure-pipelines/templates/test.yml` L35–39](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/ansible-ansible@45df14a2e05573e6213ce789aa3278f4f30fa54f/-/blob/.azure-pipelines/templates/test.yml?L35-39)

```yaml
- task: PublishPipelineArtifact@1
  condition: eq(variables.haveBotResults, 'true')
  displayName: Publish Bot Results
  inputs:
    targetPath: "$(outputPath)/bot/"
    artifactName: "Bot $(System.JobAttempt) $(System.StageDisplayName) $(System.JobDisplayName)"
```

**Interpretation:** CI is wired to detect and publish bot-specific result artifacts. The `bot/` output directory and the `haveBotResults` variable imply that `ansible-test` or a wrapper script emits structured data consumed downstream by an automation process (likely `ansibullbot` reading CI status from pipelines).

---

#### OBS-4 — `.gitattributes` excludes `.github/` from exports

**Artifact:** [`.gitattributes`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/ansible-ansible@45df14a2e05573e6213ce789aa3278f4f30fa54f/-/blob/.gitattributes)

```
.github/ export-ignore
```

**Interpretation:** The entire `.github/` directory — containing `BOTMETA.yml` and all issue/PR templates — is excluded from `git archive` exports. This is standard practice to keep bot/governance metadata out of release tarballs, but it also means bot configuration never ships in distributed artifacts.

---

#### OBS-5 — `cherry_picker` tool configured for automated backport management

**Artifact:** [`.cherry_picker.toml`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/ansible-ansible@45df14a2e05573e6213ce789aa3278f4f30fa54f/-/blob/.cherry_picker.toml)

```toml
team = "ansible"
repo = "ansible"
check_sha = "f31421576b00f0b167cdbe61217c31c21a41ac02"
fix_commit_msg = false
default_branch = "devel"
```

**Interpretation:** [`cherry_picker`](https://github.com/python/cherry-picker) is a CPython-origin tool that automates cherry-pick PRs to stable branches. Its presence configures a semi-automated backport workflow; it is bot-adjacent (a human invokes it but it creates PRs programmatically). No AI involvement.

---

#### OBS-6 — `automerge: false` as an explicit policy constraint

This deserves its own observation because it is a deterministic, machine-enforced policy signal. The top-level [`automerge: false`](https://demo.sourcegraph.com/r/github.com/sg-evals/ansible-ansible@45df14a2e05573e6213ce789aa3278f4f30fa54f/-/blob/.github/BOTMETA.yml?L1) in `BOTMETA.yml` means the bot is **not permitted to merge PRs autonomously** — human review is required for all merges. This is a hard constraint on bot agency.

---

#### OBS-7 — No AI/LLM tooling, no Copilot configuration, no generated-work disclosures

A complete scan of the repository tree reveals:
- No `.github/copilot-instructions.md` or equivalent
- No `.cursorrules`, `.clinerules`, or agent-persona files
- No `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `GEMINI.md`
- No prompt or session artifacts
- No `Co-authored-by: github-actions[bot]` or similar AI-attribution patterns in files
- No `generated by` disclosures in committed files
- The `.gitignore` does not mention any AI tool output directories

---

### Proposed Deterministic Sourcegraph Queries

These can be run across the corpus (not just this repo) to test each observation at scale.

**OBS-1 — ansibullbot robot disclosure in issue templates**
```
file:\.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ "processed automatically by a robot" "ansibullbot"
```

**OBS-2 — BOTMETA.yml existence and automerge setting**
```
file:^\.github/BOTMETA\.yml$ automerge
```
```
file:^\.github/BOTMETA\.yml$ "automerge: false"
```

**OBS-3 — Bot Results artifact in CI pipelines**
```
file:\.azure-pipelines/ OR file:\.github/workflows/ "haveBotResults" OR "bot/" "PublishPipelineArtifact"
```
```
file:\.yml$ "Publish Bot Results" "targetPath"
```

**OBS-4 — `.gitattributes` suppressing `.github/` from exports**
```
file:^\.gitattributes$ "export-ignore" ".github"
```

**OBS-5 — cherry_picker configuration**
```
file:^\.cherry_picker\.toml$
```
```
file:^\.cherry_picker\.toml$ "default_branch"
```

**OBS-6 — automerge explicitly disabled in BOTMETA**
```
file:^\.github/BOTMETA\.yml$ "automerge: false"
```
(contrast with `"automerge: true"` to find repos where the bot is permitted to merge)

**OBS-7 — Absence of AI agent instruction files (negative test)**
```
file:(^\.github/copilot-instructions\.md$|^AGENTS\.md$|^CLAUDE\.md$|^\.cursorrules$)
```
(repos that **do not** match this are candidates for absent AI configuration)

```
"Co-authored-by: github-actions" OR "generated by GPT" OR "generated by Copilot" OR "generated by Claude"
```

---

### Conclusion

At revision `45df14a2`, `ansible/ansible` contains **zero generative-AI artifacts**. The repository's automation story is entirely pre-LLM: a named triage/labelling bot (`ansibullbot`) governed by a machine-readable policy file (`BOTMETA.yml`), CI pipelines that publish structured bot result artifacts, a `cherry_picker` backport tool, and a hard policy disabling automerge. These are the only bot-adjacent signals present. All other repository metadata is conventional human-workflow tooling (IDE ignores, editor configs, standard CI).
